text: The streets of Uruk-Under-the-Sun stank of sweat, spiced lamb, hot dust, and the particular desperation that came with the end of the month. Zik preferred it that way. In a city this loud, a man could think without being overheard.
speaker: Narrator

text: Merchants shouted over one another beneath patched awnings. Donkeys pushed through the crowd with the confidence of creatures that had never once considered whether anyone else had somewhere to be. Children slipped between adult legs. Smoke from cooking fires drifted low, carrying the smell of roasted meat and burning oil. Somewhere nearby a woman was screaming at a man who had either stolen from her or married her. Zik did not stop to find out which.
speaker: Narrator

text: He moved through the market with his father's journal tucked against his ribs and the brass compass heavy in his pouch. The mark on his palm itched beneath the linen wrapping, a hot, persistent irritation that had followed him out of the tomb and refused every ordinary explanation. The third time he checked it, the shape matched the symbol on the dead king's crown exactly. He decided not to look again.
speaker: Narrator

text: That was how he handled most problems. If something refused to make sense, he gave it time to become someone else's problem.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag and Enhedu kept a respectful distance behind him. Neither had asked what he found in the tomb. Neither had asked why he went pale when he opened the journal. They had both noticed, of course. Balag noticed everything that might kill him. Enhedu noticed everything that might make her rich.
speaker: Narrator

text: The Collector waited in the back room of a wine shop that pretended to be respectable. The front room was crowded with merchants drinking watered wine beneath a faded painted sign of a smiling woman holding a cup. The woman had lost most of her face to age and smoke, but the smile remained. Zik had always thought that was a fair summary of the city.
speaker: Narrator

text: He pushed through the curtain at the back.
speaker: Narrator

text: The Collector looked up from his ledger. He was a narrow man with a narrow face, a narrow beard, and the sort of eyes that made people check whether their purses were still attached. His name had been forgotten by nearly everyone who dealt with him. That was deliberate. A man who bought stolen antiquities for a living had no use for a name people could remember.
